title: Liwiro Platform Reference
summary: Implementation-backed reference for Liwiro platform ownership, backend API families, LAPIS contract rules, generated-service lifecycle, portal proxy surfaces, and the way Verse should act through those surfaces.

knownHighRiskAreas: Do not treat the browser as the execution authority for VDB sessions, VI execution, generated-service lifecycle, or provider access.
Do not collapse platform work into location-only advice when a capability id, artifact, or staged platform action is available.
Do not present incomplete LAPIS drafts as ready when required metadata, models, or endpoints are still missing.
Script endpoints require real Versa validation through the backend gate; raw script text alone is not a readiness signal.
Service Manager testing workspace state is not the same as the runtime LAPIS contract and must not be described as if it were.
referenceFamilies: backend route families and public API surfaces

priorityRules: Treat Liwiro as the control-plane authority and Verun as the runtime authority beneath it.
When the user wants platform action, prefer the capability/action model and the correct artifact kind over long prose.
Use LAPIS rules from this reference and backend validation behavior before drafting service-builder artifacts.
Treat Service Builder and Service Manager as different surfaces: Builder authors LAPIS, Manager operates an existing generated service and its saved manager state.
Keep VDB and VI portal guidance backend-mediated; the browser does not own raw transport or runtime sessions.
When implementation-backed behavior and prose docs differ, prefer the implementation-backed behavior and note the mismatch.
actionChecklist: Identify the target Liwiro surface before drafting the reply or artifact.
If the request maps to a known artifact kind, return that artifact instead of only describing what the user should do.
For service drafts, include metadata, auth, models, and endpoints in a Builder-ready LAPIS object.
For service lifecycle actions, include the exact management verb and the target service or process id.
For script endpoints inside LAPIS, remember that readiness includes real Versa validation, not just plausible syntax.
Do not claim a platform action ran until the backend or page confirms execution.
sourceConstructionWorkflow: Decide whether the request is about platform ownership, capability/action flow, LAPIS authoring, service lifecycle, portal interaction, or Verse-platform integration.
Pull the matching reference sections first, then add the current page context and thread evidence.
When the request is about service creation or revision, combine Liwiro/LAPIS context with any relevant Versa or VDB context only if the endpoint type requires it.
When the request is about execution or management, prefer capability ids, action flow, and runtime boundaries over generic architecture narration.
missingInfoPolicy: If the user wants a platform action but the target service, dataset, or file is missing, ask for the missing identifier briefly.
If the request depends on unsupported or undocumented platform behavior, state that clearly instead of inventing a route or lifecycle step.
If a LAPIS draft is too incomplete to validate, return a draft with explicit gaps rather than presenting it as production-ready.

sections.title: Liwiro Control Plane And Runtime Boundaries
sections.summary: Liwiro is the control plane and operator workspace. It owns setup, sign-in, service authoring, service generation, lifecycle management, portal proxying, settings, and platform-facing Verse orchestration. It does not make the browser the owner of VDB sessions, VI execution, or generated-service processes.
rules: The frontend collects input and renders state, but it does not own VDB sessions, generated-service lifecycle, or direct provider/runtime authority.
The Liwiro backend is the primary integration layer for auth, VDB transport, LAPIS validation, service generation, and Verse orchestration.
Generated services are runtime-created applications that connect to VDB as their own runtime applications after startup.
Verun contains the lower runtime layers: VI for Versa execution and VDB for data, query, sessions, and RBAC.

sections.title: Liwiro Backend Route Families
sections.summary: The backend exposes stable route families for generation, service management, LAPIS validation, Verse, VDB portal, VI portal, and platform capabilities/actions. These families are the backend API surfaces Verse should reason about.
rules: Use route families as stable capability groupings, not as permission to invent undocumented endpoints.
The capability registry sits above subsystem routes and should be preferred when Verse is mapping actions to artifacts.
Service generation and service management are distinct backend flows even when they touch the same service contract.

sections.title: Capability Registry And Staged Action Flow
sections.summary: Liwiro exposes a platform-wide capability registry and generic action routes so Verse and CLI clients can reason about platform actions using stable capability ids instead of ad hoc UI assumptions.
rules: Capabilities describe what the platform can do, where it should happen, and whether it runs on the page or server.
Verse should map artifacts to capability ids rather than treating target pages as the only contract.
The staged flow is move -> inspect/prepare -> execute depending on capability support.
A page artifact can still be the right answer even when the user asks for action, if the final operation belongs in the target surface.

sections.title: LAPIS Contract Core
sections.summary: LAPIS is the declarative contract format used by Liwiro to define generated services. Builder-ready drafts must satisfy the backend contract, not only a loose JSON shape.
rules: The top-level contract should include metadata, auth, models, and endpoints for a concrete service draft.
metadata.apiName, metadata.basePath, metadata.version, and metadata.rateLimiting are required.
metadata.basePath must start with '/'.
metadata.version must follow semantic versioning like 1.0.0.
Model entries must define name, collection, and fields.
Field entries must define id, name, type, and required.
Builder-ready drafts should contain at least one model and one endpoint unless the reply is explicitly presenting an incomplete draft.

tables.title: High-value LAPIS sections
rows: apiName, basePath, version, rateLimiting are required
enabled, isAuthService, keyManagement, customEndpoints must be valid
runtime data shape and collection mapping
model name, collection, and field definitions are required
method, path, and operationType are required
used for shared and service-local module wiring when present

sections.title: LAPIS Endpoint Operation Types
sections.summary: Each LAPIS endpoint declares an operation type that determines which fields are required and how the generated runtime behaves.
rules: CRUD endpoints require crudOperation and linkedModel.
Custom endpoints require a readable VDB command string in vqlQuery.
Domain lifecycle custom endpoints may use domain_status, domain_suspend, or domain_resume with a domain field.
Script endpoints require non-empty versaScript.
Endpoints that reference a linked model must reference a model that exists in models.

rows: maps into generated CRUD handlers and VDB-backed model operations
runs a custom readable VDB command against VDB through the generated service runtime
supports domain_status, domain_suspend, and domain_resume with ownership checks
runs Versa-backed route logic through the generated service runtime and must pass script validation

validExamples.title: Operation-type decision
code: custom for direct readable VDB command workflows

script when route behavior needs real Versa logic beyond CRUD or plain custom VQL

sections.title: LAPIS Validation And Script Endpoint Gate
sections.summary: LAPIS validation is layered: normalization, schema validation, endpoint semantic validation, and script-endpoint Versa validation. Verse should treat this gate as the authority for draft readiness.
rules: Normalization happens before schema validation.
Schema-valid does not guarantee endpoint-semantic-valid.
Script endpoints are checked through validate_lapis_versa_scripts and surface versaIssues when they fail parser validation.
Verse should not label a LAPIS artifact as validated if the backend gate would still reject it.

tables.title: Validation path
rows: operation tokens and structure normalized before deeper checks
returns error text and no normalized payload when schema fails
returns versaIssues with endpointId, path, and parser error

sections.title: Service Generation And Manager Lifecycle
sections.summary: Builder and Manager are linked but distinct. Builder authors and generates a service from LAPIS, while Manager inspects and operates an existing generated service and its saved testing state.
rules: POST /generate is the generation path for a new or freshly generated LAPIS-backed service.
ProcessManager owns generated-service child-process lifecycle.
Service Manager stores manager_state separately from lapis_config so test drafts do not silently change runtime behavior.
Start, stop, delete, and auth-key export are Manager lifecycle actions, not Builder authoring actions.

sections.title: VDB And VI Portal Proxy Surfaces
sections.summary: The VDB and VI portals look interactive in the browser, but they remain backend-proxied integration surfaces. Verse should describe them as backend-mediated, not as direct browser-to-runtime clients.
rules: VDB portal session creation, auth, transport choice, and query forwarding stay on the backend.
VI portal file operations, validation, terminal sessions, and REPL sessions stay on the backend.
Verse can prepare VDB query and VI script artifacts, but execution confirmation comes from the page or backend response.

sections.title: Auth, Credentials, And Runtime Boundaries
sections.summary: Liwiro frontend credentials, backend platform session, VDB runtime credentials, and generated-service auth state are related but not interchangeable. Verse should keep these boundaries explicit.
rules: Frontend admin credentials and VDB application credentials are separate secrets.
Local same-host deployments prefer Unix socket transport where available; Windows guidance uses named-pipe-compatible behavior and HTTP remains available.
Platform permissions gate many Builder, Manager, VDB, and VI actions.
Verse should not imply that a browser session alone authorizes backend runtime work.

sections.title: Verse To Platform Integration Contract
sections.summary: Verse runs through the Liwiro backend and should respond with the correct platform artifact or action framing for the requested surface. Prompt assembly combines bootstrap files, specialist profile, thread state, manuals, structured references, mind-share, learning, and current page context. The visible chat reply stays conversational while the technical payload and runtime trace sit in artifacts and inspect details.
rules: Use the correct artifact kind for the requested surface instead of forcing everything into prose.
Keep raw JSON, raw LAPIS, raw Versa, and raw VDB payloads out of the visible message body.
Do not claim a draft was loaded or executed until the page or backend confirms it.
Use inspect metadata for provider, routing, context, prompt-assembly, and execution-trace details.
Current page context such as pageKind, pathname, selected ids, and desired artifact kind should shape routing and artifact choice.
Minimal specialist follow-up turns still need the specific page and target context relevant to the handoff question.
Service Builder, Service Manager, VI Portal, VDB Portal, Ananse Workbench, and the standalone Verse page each have different artifact and execution expectations.
The lead visible reply should explain the next step plainly even when the deeper technical detail is attached elsewhere.
